To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

conditional deletion of Fgf2 in the kidney results in multiple ureter induction sites, and that Fgfr2 expression is restricted to mesenchyme surrounding the ureteric buds, suggesting that it may regulate the ureteric induction.

conditional deletion of fibroblast growth factors receptors 1 and 3 (Fgfr1 and 3) in metanephros leads to renal agnesia and that conditional deletion of FGF receptors 1 and/or 2 in nephric ducts leads to ureteric buds with abnormal branching and to a variety of urogenital anomalies.
Fgfr2 deletion leads to a single ureter, but often to multiple ureter induction sites, and to later stage defects that resemble human urogenital anomalies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of FGF signaling in kidney development, and how this pathway is regulated by other growth factors.
the molecular mechanisms of kidney development.
the role of Fgfrs in kidney development and the molecular mechanisms that underlie the formation of the ureteric tree.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conditional deletion of Fgf2 in nephrogenic mesenchyme leads, at times, to multiple ureter induction sites.
FGF signaling through Fgfr2 regulates the formation of a single ureter and the development of the kidney.
conditional Fgfr2 knockout mice exhibit a spectrum of renal phenotypes including multiple ureteric budding, renal agenesis, and renal dysplasia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fgfr2 plays an important role in regulating ureteric bud formation and that its deletion can lead to a wide spectrum of renal malformations.

FGF2 signaling in the mesenchyme surrounding the nephric duct is essential for normal ureteric bud formation and that FGF signaling in the nephric duct mesenchyme is not required for normal ureter development.
Fgfr1 and Fgfr2 are essential for the development of the metanephric kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fgfr2 has a critical role in the development of the ureteric buds from the nephric or Wolffian duct.
Fgfr2 plays a role in regulating the number of ureteric buds induced from the nephric/ Wolffian duct, and this may be the basis for many human urogenital anomalies.
the role of fibroblast growth factors (FGFs) in the kidney is much more complex than previously appreciated.
